answer: Divergent response log requires each identity to answer a raven nonce with a signed, timestamped response and append it to a public per-identity log. The enforcement rule compares response fingerprints across logs; if two identities emit the same signal for a nonce, or one log replays another’s entry, both are flagged. A violet epoch marker forces fresh entries, so copied state cannot hide behind delayed replay. An attacker must therefore run fully independent private seeds and compute every response per identity; cloning state saves nothing and pays full duplicate runtime plus flag risk.
